fields.meta_title: Free Wine Quiz and Builder for Shops and Clubs | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Take a free wine quiz that matches you to crisp white, rich white, light red, or bold red. Then build one for a shop, club, bistro, or bar.
fields.h1: Build a Wine Quiz That Sends Every Guest to the Right Bottle
fields.hero_description: Build a wine quiz that matches each guest to a wine style and its bottles, or take the eight-question version below.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for a Wine Quiz
fields.features_subheading: A single prompt writes the questions, the four result screens, and the table that keeps every finish. Ask again to change any of them.
fields.feature_1:
Every option points at one wine style

Tell Emergent which styles you pour, such as crisp white and bold red. It drafts questions about food and drink habits, and every answer choice counts toward one of those matches.
fields.feature_2:
Bottles listed on the result screen

Tag each label in your catalog with one style. The result screen lists every wine carrying that tag, with names and prices the app reads from your store through its API.
fields.feature_3:
A scored mode for staff wine tests

Turn on scoring for server training. Each question carries one right answer, a server below your pass mark gets a retake, and every miss shows the answer they should have picked.
fields.feature_4:
An alert the moment a quiz is finished

Send an email or a Slack message on every finish. A cellar manager learns which wines to pack for a new member, and a trainer gets the day's server scores before service.
fields.feature_5:
A leaderboard that moves as teams answer

Run trivia night on phones, one question per screen for each team, while a live leaderboard updates on the bar's TV. No response cap applies, however full the room gets.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code on paid plans

Put the quiz on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans add full code export to your GitHub repository, for next season's list.

Every Light Red match opens on three bottles

Clementine Rauch finishes the quiz on Marrowbank Wine Shop's site with a Light Red match. Her result screen lists the 3 bottles the shop tagged Light Red, each priced from the store catalog. Her answers and email go into the customer table.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Wine Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a wine quiz that matches guests to a style and keeps every finish in a table you own.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Map every option to one result
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tag each bottle with one style
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what a result hands the taker: a bottle to buy, a box to ship, or a score to clear. This page's quiz sorts takers into four styles, two white and two red, and every question has to split them among those four.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Takers know what they eat and drink, not how a wine was made. Ask how they take their tea, whether they squeeze lemon on fish, and what is on the plate. Strong black tea stands in for tannin, the phenolic compounds that add bitterness to wine.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each option so it belongs to a single style, and keep the options in a set the same kind and length. An option that fits two styles blurs the match. Give every style options in at least 2 questions, or no taker can reach it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For a shop or a club, give every bottle in the catalog exactly one style tag and let the result screen list whatever carries it. The app reads names and prices from the store through its API, and a new bottle joins its style once tagged.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send every finish to one table, with the email kept beside the result it came with. Route alerts from that table: an email to the cellar manager for a club box, or the day's score list for the trainer before service.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Source each answer in a scored test
fields.howto_step_6_des: A style finder has no wrong answers, but a staff test or a trivia night does. Mark one correct option per question, set the pass mark, and check each answer against a written source before the first server or team plays.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Play it once per result before launch
fields.howto_step_7_des: Take the quiz four times, aiming each run at a different style, and confirm the match lands where you expect. Then open the row it wrote and the email it sent. Change anything off by prompt, then play it through again.

faq_plan.a: A wine quiz is a short set of questions that either matches the taker to a wine style or tests what they know about wine. Shops and clubs run the matching kind as a bottle finder, while bistros and bars score the other kind for staff training and trivia. The quiz above asks eight questions and names one of four styles.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a wine quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI survey builder: the styles you want as results and where each finish should go. Emergent builds the quiz and its database from that prompt, and you change any part by prompting again. Start with the results, since every question has to point at one of them.

faq_plan.q: Can I put a free wine quiz on my shop's website?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing. Put the quiz on the homepage or beside the bottles it recommends, and keep it under 10 questions so a shopper finishes before drifting back to browsing.

faq_plan.q: What makes good wine quiz questions for beginners?
faq_plan.a: Questions about everyday taste work best, because a beginner can answer them without wine vocabulary. Ask whether they squeeze lemon over fish: acidity tastes tart and zesty, in food and in a glass. Ask how dark they like their chocolate, and leave grape names and regions out entirely.

faq_plan.q: How do I write wine quiz questions and answers I can trust?
faq_plan.a: Take every answer from a written source and keep the source's own words next to the question. One example: full-bodied wines typically have more tannin, higher alcohol, and dark fruit flavors such as black currant. Then write three wrong options of the same kind, so the right one never stands out by its length.

faq_plan.q: Should my wine quiz match a style or keep score?
faq_plan.a: Match a style when the taker is a shopper or a club member: options point at results, and no answer is wrong. Keep score when a trainer or a trivia host reads the numbers, with one correct option per question. Emergent builds either kind from a prompt, and a follow-up prompt switches between them.

faq_plan.q: How many styles should a wine quiz have as results?
faq_plan.a: Four is a workable start: two whites and two reds, one lighter and one fuller in each color. Add rosé or sparkling only when you stock enough of it to fill a result screen. Drop any style that leads to nothing you sell or pour.

faq_plan.q: What should a wine quiz result say about the style?
faq_plan.a: Name the style first, then give one line on why the answers point there, then show the bottles. Light reds are known for lighter tannin, bright acidity, and red fruit flavors, which tells a taker who chose tart cranberry over dark chocolate why they landed there. End on the bottles tagged for that style.

faq_plan.q: How do I use a wine quiz to train servers on a new list?
faq_plan.a: Write the questions from the new list's own tasting notes, one correct option each, and set the pass mark before anyone sits it. Add a question on why a rich white tastes of vanilla or coconut: oak aging adds that note, and guests ask about it at the table.

faq_plan.q: When should a wine quiz ask for the taker's email?
faq_plan.a: Ask on the last screen, after the final question and before the result. Make it optional on a tasting-room tablet and required for a club sign-up, where the email ties the result to the member's first box. In an Emergent quiz the address sits beside its result in a database you own, and no response cap applies.

quiz.title: Which Wine Style Fits Your Taste?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about food and drink you already know, no wine words needed. At the end you get one of four styles: crisp white, rich white, light red, or bold red.

questions.text: What lands on your plate on a good Friday night?

options.text: Roast chicken with a cream sauce
Pink, with a splash of cranberry
I would rather have a cola

questions.explanation: Sour lemonade fans tend to like tart wines. Acidity in food and drink tastes tart and zesty, and crisp whites carry plenty of it.

source.quote: Acidity in food and drink tastes tart and zesty.

questions.text: How do you take your tea?

options.text: Black, left in until it is strong

questions.explanation: Strong black tea is a stand-in for tannin. Tannin in wine is the presence of phenolic compounds that add bitterness, and bold reds carry the most.

source.quote: Tannin in wine is the presence of phenolic compounds that add bitterness to a wine.

questions.text: Which chocolate do you reach for?

options.text: The darkest bar on the shelf

questions.text: Where would you drink a glass right now?

options.text: By a fire with a book
At a picnic in the park
At a long dinner with friends

questions.text: Which fruit bowl do you pick from first?
How cold do you like your drinks?

options.text: Ice cold, straight from the fridge

questions.text: Pick a snack for the table.

results.title: Crisp White
results.description: Your answers lean toward tart, cold, and refreshing. Look for light-bodied dry whites, and drink them young, within a year or two of the vintage, while the fruit is fresh. Serve them straight from the fridge with seafood and salads.

results.title: Rich White
results.description: You picked creamy, mellow, and comforting answers. Look for full-bodied whites, where oak aging adds a vanilla or coconut note. Serve them cool rather than ice cold. They sit well beside roast chicken or a cream sauce.

results.title: Light Red
results.description: Your answers lean toward red fruit and a light touch. Light reds are known for lighter tannin and bright acidity, so they suit mushrooms, poultry, and a picnic. A slight chill before pouring suits them too.

results.title: Bold Red
results.description: You chose dark, strong, and savory answers. Full-bodied reds typically carry more tannin, higher alcohol, and dark fruit such as black currant, and they stand up to steak, barbecue, and aged cheese.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits between retailers' style finders and wine trivia pages, and none shows how to build either one. This page lets a visitor play an eight-question wine quiz that matches them to crisp white, rich white, light red, or bold red from everyday food and drink habits, then shows four wine businesses using one: an online shop that lists the bottles tagged for a result, a winery club that fills a first shipment from it, a bistro that scores servers before a new list, and a wine bar that runs trivia night on phones with a live leaderboard. Every finish lands in a database the owner keeps. The FAQ covers question writing, free use, trivia answers, scoring, result count, bottle tagging, and email capture.
